text: Because all I had read were books in which characters were foreign, I had become convinced that books, by their very nature, had to have foreigners in them, and had to be about things with which I could not personally identify. <break time="0.8s" /> Now, things changed when I discovered African books. <break time="0.8s" /> There were not many of them available. <break time="0.8s" /> And they were not quite as easy to find as the foreign books. <break time="0.8s" /> But because of writers like Chinua Achebe and Camara Laye, I went through a mental shift in my perception of literature. <break time="0.8s" /> I realized that people like me, girls with skin the color of chocolate, whose kinky hair could not form ponytails, could also exist in literature. <break time="0.8s" /> I started to write about things I recognized. <break time="0.8s" /> Now, I loved those American and British books I read. <break time="0.8s" /> They stirred my imagination. <break time="0.8s" /> They opened up new worlds for me. <break time="0.8s" /> But the unintended consequence was that I did not know that people like me could exist in literature. <break time="0.8s" /> So what the discovery of African writers did for me was this, it saved me from having a single story of what books are. <break time="0.8s" /> I come from a conventional, middle class Nigerian family. <break time="0.8s" /> My father was a professor. <break time="0.8s" /> My mother was an administrator. <break time="0.8s" /> And so we had, as was the norm, live in domestic help, who would often come from nearby rural villages. <break time="0.8s" /> So the year I turned eight we got a new house boy. <break time="0.8s" /> His name was Fide. <break time="0.8s" /> The only thing my mother told us about him was that his family was very poor. <break time="0.8s" /> My mother sent yams and rice, and our old clothes, to his family. <break time="0.8s" /> And when I did not finish my dinner, my mother would say, Finish your food, Do you not know, People like Fides family have nothing. <break time="0.8s" /> So I felt enormous pity for Fides family.
